unsupported_claims: The trade-off is between expressiveness/representational power and tractability, rather than computational efficiency and predictive accuracy.
Supervised procedures have lower training-time complexity per task; the evidence says they have high training time complexity.
Unsupervised procedures generally require more training time (layer-wise or two-stage pipelines); the evidence says they are computationally efficient.
Unsupervised predictive accuracy is often lower than supervised; the evidence says a carefully designed objective closely matches task-specific accuracy.
rationale: The answer reverses the paper's central comparison: it claims supervised training is cheaper and unsupervised training is slower, whereas the evidence says supervised is costly and unsupervised is efficient. It also misstates the trade-off, which the paper frames as computational efficiency versus predictive accuracy.
